A pacemaker is present in the right anterior chest wall. Its leads extend to the right ventricular apex. The trachea and both main bronchi are midline. The airway lumina are patent and free of obstructive pathology.

Mediastinal assessment is limited on this noncontrast examination. As visualized, the thoracic aorta is normal in caliber. The pulmonary trunk and both pulmonary arteries measure 33 mm and 28 mm, respectively. The heart is enlarged. The pericardium is normal in thickness, without effusion. Atherosclerotic wall calcifications involve the thoracic aorta and coronary arteries. An aortic valve prosthesis is present. A well-circumscribed benign cystic lesion measuring 27x23x36 mm is present in the anterior mediastinum at the interface of the ascending aorta and pulmonary trunk. The thoracic esophagus is normal in caliber, without significant masslike wall thickening. The prevascular, pre-paratracheal, subcarinal, bilateral hilar, and bilateral axillary lymph nodes are not pathologically enlarged.

A mosaic attenuation pattern is present in both lungs. This may reflect small airway disease or small vessel disease. Linear subsegmental atelectatic changes involve the right middle lobe, the lingula of the left upper lobe, and the basal segments of both lower lobes. Peribronchial thickening is bilateral. Interlobular septal thickening is more prominent in the right middle lobe and basal lower-lobe segments. I favor cardiac stasis as the primary explanation for these changes.

A subpleural nodular ground-glass opacity is present in the posterior subsegment of the apicoposterior segment of the left upper lobe. The appearance is nonspecific. It may be compatible with viral pneumonias, especially coronavirus disease 2019 pneumonia. Clinical and laboratory correlation is recommended. A 14x10 mm subpleural nodular area of consolidation is present in the posterobasal segment of the right lower lobe. The differential includes round pneumonia and round atelectasis. Follow-up of this right lower lobe consolidation is recommended. Millimetric nonspecific parenchymal nodules are present in both lungs. The lung parenchyma is free of a discrete mass. Sequela-type thickening involves the bilateral posterior costal pleura.

The gallbladder and right kidney are not visible on the included images, consistent with surgery. The right adrenal gland corpus is thickened. A 29x24mm nodular mass in the left adrenal gland has a density of 6 HU and is consistent with an adenoma. The pancreas is normal. Diffuse calcific atheromatous plaques involve the abdominal aorta and its visceral branches, especially the splenic artery.

Diffuse osteodegenerative changes involve the thoracic vertebrae. The mid-thoracic disc spaces are significantly narrowed.

- Thyroid: Bilateral lobar hypertrophy. Mild bilateral parenchymal heterogeneity.
- Mediastinal vessels: PA caliber normal. Ascending and descending thoracic aortic calibers normal. Aortic arch measures 29 mm, at the upper physiologic limit. Mediastinal vascular atherosclerosis.
- Mediastinal LNs: Multiple millimetric LNs. Largest LN in the paraesophageal-subcarinal region measures approximately 25 x 11 mm. It cannot be clearly separated from the esophagus on noncontrast CT. Direct increase in dimensions.
- Central thorax: Hemithoraces symmetric. Tracheal and main bronchial calibers normal. Thoracic esophageal caliber normal. No significant tumoral wall thickening.
- Airways and interstitium: Persistent peribronchial sheath thickening, greatest in the bilateral mid-lower lung zones. Bilateral pulmonary sequelae. Peripheral interlobular and subpleural septal thickening. Slight associated GGO. If assessing for interstitial fibrosis, I recommend clinical and laboratory correlation.
- Right lung: Right apical pleuroparenchymal sequelae with traction bronchiectasis. Stable amorphous calcification caudally in the anterior segment of the RUL.
- Right pleural space: New basal pleural effusion measuring 20 mm at its thickest portion. New mild adjacent atelectasis.
- Upper abdomen: Prominent left hepatic and caudate lobes. Perihepatic and perisplenic effusions. Perihepatic effusion remains evident. Splenomegaly. Millimetric gallbladder-neck calculus, not previously clearly identified. Pancreas normal. Bilateral adrenal glands normal. If chronic liver parenchymal disease is clinically considered, I recommend liver evaluation.
- Kidneys and mesentery: Bilaterally reduced renal size. Lobulated bilateral renal contours. CRF remains a consideration. Mesenteric fat stranding.
- Anterior diaphragmatic region: Bilateral LNs. Largest LN on the right measures 21 x 13 mm. Surrounding soft-tissue planes normal.
- Osseous structures: Dorsal kyphosis. Squared vertebral bodies. Thickened, dense paravertebral longitudinal ligaments. I consider these findings suggestive of spondyloarthropathy.

The trachea and left main bronchus are patent; the right main bronchus is completely obliterated by the extensive right thoracic masses. The heart and main mediastinal vascular structures are displaced to the left. Pericardial effusion is not seen, and the left pleural effusion has completely resolved. The thoracic aorta and thoracic esophagus are normal in caliber (without significant tumor-related esophageal wall thickening). No pathologically enlarged LNs are identified in the prevascular, preparatracheal, subcarinal, bilateral hilar, or bilateral axillary stations.

On lung windows, bulky nodular masses almost completely fill the right lung and right hemithorax, extend into the mediastinum and intercostal spaces, tend to encircle the trachea, completely surround the right pulmonary artery (RPA), completely obliterate the right main bronchus, erase the fat planes between the right and left atria, and encircle the aortic arch. Slight right lung re-aeration is present, although aeration remains minimal and limited to the right upper lobe (RUL). New patchy ground-glass opacities (GGOs) in a crazy-paving pattern involve the left lung (upper-lobe predominant), consistent with a new infectious process. Multiple unchanged metastatic masses involve the right anterior chest wall (up to 55 mm).

Evaluation of the upper abdominal organs is suboptimal because they are only partially included (important examination limitation). No space-occupying lesion is seen in the included liver. The bilateral adrenal glands are normal, without a space-occupying lesion. No abnormality is seen in the included osseous structures, and the vertebral body heights are preserved.

Chronic white-matter disease: Several T2/FLAIR-hyperintense chronic ischemic gliotic lesions involve the subcortical and deep WM of both frontoparietal lobes.

Basal ganglia: Millimetric low-signal foci are present on GRE sequences in the bilateral basal ganglia, accompanied by increased perivascular spaces. I consider the low signal potentially related to calcification or iron deposition.

Remaining supratentorial structures: Midline structures maintain normal form and location. The bilateral hippocampi and parahippocampi, thalami, and internal and external capsules demonstrate normal morphology and signal intensity.

Posterior fossa and cisternal structures: The craniocervical junction and basal cisterns are normal. The cerebellar hemispheres, medulla oblongata, pons, and midbrain demonstrate normal morphology and signal intensity. The fourth ventricle is normal in width and morphology. The bilateral CPA cisterns and the intracanalicular and extracanalicular components of the CN VII/VIII complexes are symmetric and normal.

Orbits and sellar region: Both globes, retrobulbar fat planes, optic nerves, optic chiasm, cavernous sinuses, and sellar and parasellar structures are normal.

Vascular and diffusion assessment: Intracranial major vascular flow signals are normal, and the dural sinuses are patent. No acute ischemic infarct is present on DWI.

Extracranial findings: Mastoid-cell effusion (mastoiditis). Mucosal thickening involves the maxillary sinuses and ethmoid air cells. A mucus-retention cyst is present in the inferior aspect of the left maxillary sinus, and the right inferior nasal concha is hypertrophied.

cases.findings:
Clinical context and comparison: In the setting of an operated craniopharyngioma under follow-up, the sellar and suprasellar abnormality is characterized below. Comparison is made with CT dated [date_1].

Sellar/suprasellar region and ventricular system: A recurrent heterogeneous craniopharyngioma measuring approximately 36x26 mm fills the sellar and suprasellar cisterns and extends into the third ventricle, resulting in narrowing and obstruction of the third ventricle. The mass size is increased compared to the previous examination. The pituitary gland remains separately discernible inferior to the mass. The optic chiasm and both anterior cerebral artery (ACA) A1 segments are displaced anteriorly. Enlargement of the bilateral lateral ventricles and third ventricle is present and was also present on the examination from the early postoperative period.

Ischemic-gliotic and postinterventional changes: Sequela ischemic-gliotic foci involve the bilateral periventricular white matter, corona radiata, and centrum semiovale. A defective appearance of the corpus callosum is attributable to old intervention.

Left maxillary sinus and adjacent structures: A mass fills the left maxillary sinus and extends into the nasal cavity adjacent to the left inferior nasal concha, with an associated defect of the medial wall of the left maxillary sinus. Superiorly, defects involve the upper wall of the left maxillary sinus and the inferior orbital wall, accompanied by minimal intraorbital soft-tissue extension. Additional bone defects involve the lateral wall of the left maxilla and, inferiorly, the pterygoid bone. The mass has malignant features in appearance, invades the hard palate, and demonstrates anterior soft-tissue extension at the left maxillary body. This mass was absent on the [date_2] examination.

Additional observations: Left mastoiditis is present. Apart from the specifically described defects, the remaining cranial osseous structures are normal. Both globes, the retrobulbar fat, and both optic nerves are normal. The optic chiasm is otherwise normal in appearance despite the anterior displacement described above.

cases.findings:
Cardiomediastinal/Airways: Mediastinal assessment suboptimal on unenhanced MDCT. Trachea and bilateral main bronchi patent, without endoluminal obstructive lesion. Calcified atherosclerotic change in the thoracic aortic wall. Main mediastinal vessels and cardiac size/contour normal. No pericardial effusion or thickening. Thoracic esophagus normal in caliber, without significant mural thickening. Sliding hiatal hernia. No pathologically enlarged or morphologically abnormal mediastinal or bilateral hilar lymph nodes.

Lungs/Pleura: 16 mm air cyst in the right lower lobe (RLL). Minimal pleuroparenchymal sequelae densities in the middle zone of the right lung and inferior lingular segment of the left lung. No pulmonary mass or infiltrate. No pleural thickening or effusion bilaterally.

Upper Abdomen: Visualized upper abdominal organs unremarkable. No space-occupying lesion in the visualized liver. Bilateral adrenal glands normal, without space-occupying lesion.

Osseous Structures: Degenerative changes. Thoracic kyphosis has increased. Reticular osseous density increases due to osteopenia.
